title: Germany – Urban planning and landscape architectural services – Freiraum- und verkehrsplanerischer Planungswettbewerb für den Arnulf-Klett-Platz in Stuttgart
description: Mit der Inbetriebnahme des neuen Stuttgarter Tiefbahnhofs und den damit verbundenen Veränderungen im Bahnhofsumfeld ergeben sich weitreichende Chancen für eine Neuordnung des öffentlichen Raums rund um den Hauptbahnhof. Davon ist insbesondere der Arnulf-Klett-Platz betroffen. Ziel des Planungswettbewerbs ist es, den Charakter des Arnulf-Klett-Platzes neu zu definieren und eine zeitgemäße freiraum- und verkehrsplanerische Gesamtkonzeption für den Platz und die Schillerstraße zu entwickeln. Das Dokument "Gegenstand und Ziel", welches den Vergabeunterlagenbeigefügt ist, enthält weitere Informationen.

description: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) intends to contract using other than full and open competition for a fiber optic lease that ensures TSA maintains fiber optic connectivity at Pittsburgh International Airport (PIT) . Accordingly, the TSA intends to award purchase order to at the Allegheny County Airport Authority (ACAA). This purchase order will address the requirements of the TSA Information Technology(IT)/ End User Services Division (EUSD). TSA intends to award this requirement under the authority of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 13.106-1(b)(2) for a period of five (5) years (one-year base period and four one-year option periods). TSA requires a lease for four (4) strands of fiber optic multi-mode strands to ensure continuous TSA network connectivity for TSA personnel in TSA occupied space at SFB. This synopsis is not a request for competitive quotes. It is a notice that outlines the Government's intent to contract on a sole source basis with SAA. Sources may identify their interest and capability by responding to this notice. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. In doing so, interested sources must submit detailed technical capabilities and any other information that demonstrates their ability to meet the needs of the Government. Detailed capabilities must be submitted by email to Stacey Davis Stacey.Davis@tsa.dhs.gov in an electronic format, no later than December 2, 2026 at 12:00PM Local Time (Arlington, VA). All information shall be furnished at no cost or obligation to the Government. Responses shall be limited to no more than two (2) pages. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. This synopsis is not to be considered a request for quotations or proposals but is displaying the Government's intent to pursue a sole source strategy for this acquisition. Interested vendors who may wish to seek subcontracting opportunities should contact the above named airport directly.

title: J059--Intent to Sole Source-Police Harris Radio Maintenance James A Haley Veterans Hospital
description: In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, the James A. Haley VA Medical Center intends to negotiate a sole-source award with **Communications International, Inc.**, located at 2150 15th Ave Vero Beach, FL 32960 USA. Communications International Inc. is the authorized L3Harris channel partner assigned to provide sales, service, and warranty support for the L3Harris 700/800 MHz and P25 radio system. Critical capabilities supporting the sole-source determination include: Routine and emergency communications at the James A. Haley VAMC and its Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCS). The system utilizes the Hillsborough County Sherriff s Office s (HCSO) L3Harris radio infrastructure and radio towers installed throughout Hillsborough County. The VA Police has an Interlocal Mutual Agreement with HCSO to use their infrastructure. This agreement requires the VA to annually align microwave equipment, perform software upgrades, and perform all scheduled and/or emergency repairs associated with the 700/800 MHz, P25, microwave equipment, ancillary sub-systems, and antenna systems. This requirement covers the required maintenance of the radio system at the James A. Haley VA Medical Center, located at **13000 Bruce B. Downs Blvd, Tampa, FL 33612**. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is **811210-Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance**, with a size standard of **$34 million dollars**. **This notice of intent is not a request for quotations. ** Interested parties that believe they possess the capability and qualifications to meet these requirements may identify their interest and submit capability statements. All submissions must be received no later than **12:00 PM EST on December 2ND, 2026**. Information submitted in response to this notice will be provided at no cost or obligation to the Government.� No formal solicitation will be issued. Interested parties must submit their information by email to Katrina Tavares, Contracting Officer, at **katrina.tavares@va.gov**. Responses received will be evaluated; however, the Government reserves the right to proceed with the sole-source negotiation with Communications International Inc. if no acceptable responses are received. The determination not to compete this proposed procurement is at the sole discretion of the Government.

description: The due date for receipt of proposals is extended to allow the Government sufficient time to prepare and release responses to questions received from prospective offerors. Notice of VISN-Based Solicitation Structure Since release of the prior draft solicitation, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) has refined the acquisition strategy for Real Estate Acquisition Support Services to align with the Veterans Health Administration�s (VHA) evolving regional operating model. This revised approach supports VA�s broader Restructure for Impact and Sustainability Effort (RISE), an organizational transformation directed by Executive Order 14210. RISE is intended to streamline VHA structures and processes, strengthen regional implementation and accountability, and support more consistent, coordinated, and responsive services for Veterans. Accordingly, VA has transitioned from a single nationwide contractor-pool approach to a multiple-award IDIQ structure organized by Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) Coverage Area. Benefits of the VISN-based approach include: Allowing qualified SDVOSB offerors to compete for one or more VISN Coverage Areas rather than requiring a nationwide proposal; Enabling offerors to focus proposals on geographic areas where they can demonstrate staffing, local-market resources, capacity, and lawful authority to operate; Supporting focused competition and VISN-specific commission pricing; Improving alignment between broker support, VA regional lease-acquisition operations, and local-market requirements; Strengthening accountability for contractor capacity, performance, quality control, and continuity of services within each VISN Coverage Area; and Supporting VA�s broader effort to simplify operations, improve consistency, and enable more effective implementation at the regional and local levels. VA considered feedback received during the draft-solicitation/RFI phase. However, because the solicitation has been materially revised since the draft-solicitation/RFI phase, VA is not posting the historical draft-stage questions and Government responses. Those historical responses may not reflect the requirements, proposal instructions, evaluation approach, or procedures in the final solicitation. The final solicitation, its attachments, and any written amendments issued by the Contracting Officer are the only authoritative sources for solicitation requirements. title: Long-Term Pavement Performance (LTPP) Program Engineering Services Contract (LPES)
description: This Synopsis is issued in accordance with FAR Part 5.203 in response to the mandatory requirement for a 15-day pre-solicitation notification. The purpose of this Synopsis is to announce the Federal Highway Administration�s (FHWA) intent to issue a solicitation for a Full and Open Competition to provide highly specialized engineering services, including field survey operations, data quality management, scientific data curation, and technology transfer support services for the LTPP program and related highway infrastructure research initiatives. FHWA contemplates award of one or more Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity contracts to successfully carry out the technical support services detailed in the Statement of Work (SOW). Offerors must demonstrate technical capability in at least one (1) Task Area to be eligible for a Base ID/IQ contract award. The anticipated period of performance shall not exceed 60 months for the ID/IQ contracts. This Synopsis is issued in accordance with FAR Part 5.203 in response to the mandatory requirement for a 15-day pre-solicitation notification. The purpose of this Synopsis is to announce the Federal Highway Administration�s (FHWA) intent to issue a solicitation for a Full and Open Competition to provide highly specialized engineering services, including field survey operations, data quality management, scientific data curation, and technology transfer support services for the LTPP program and related highway infrastructure research initiatives. FHWA contemplates award of one or more Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity contracts to successfully carry out the technical support services detailed in the Statement of Work (SOW). Offerors must demonstrate technical capability in at least one (1) Task Area to be eligible for a Base ID/IQ contract award. The anticipated period of performance shall not exceed 60 months for the ID/IQ contracts. The main objective of this contract is to provide highly specialized engineering services, including field survey operations, data quality management, scientific data curation, and technology transfer support services for the LTPP program and related highway infrastructure research initiatives. This requirement demands comprehensive technical expertise spanning pavement, bridge, and other highway infrastructure engineering, as well as advanced data systems: Specifically, the LPES contract vehicle is structured to achieve the following overarching strategic objectives: Execute comprehensive pavement condition data collection, incorporating high-speed 3D surface condition profiling (3D APCS), continuous traffic-speed deflection testing, under a rigorous Data Quality Management Plan (DQMP) to ensure defensible and research-grade data quality. Formulate strategic pavement research plans advancing the LTPP program, conduct targeted performance case studies, and deliver practical engineering tools, Section 508-compliant publications, and technical webinars. Develop and curate specialized, analysis-ready datasets for machine learning (ML) and predictive modeling across LTPP and broader highway infrastructure domains, integrating modern database architectures and coordinating data schemas with web portal contractors for public release. To fulfill the LTPP program mission and support broader FHWA pavement and other infrastructure research, the scope of work is organized across three (3) primary Task Areas. Contractors are not required to perform across all Task Areas unless awarded task orders in those areas: Task Area A � Data Collection and Processing: The Contractor shall provide all labor, contractor-owned survey vehicles, specialized diagnostic equipment, materials, and traffic control services necessary to perform automated high-speed 3D surface condition profiling, as well as deflection testing using the Traffic-Speed Deflection Device (TSDD) and Falling Weight Deflectometer (FWD) methods. Work also includes executing a comprehensive Data Quality Management Plan (DQMP), performing ground-truth equipment calibrations, field validations, and routine sensor verifications, conducting relational database processing, and delivering verified data for public portal ingestion. Task Area B � Pavement Performance Data Analysis and Product Development: The Contractor shall perform pavement research analytics, review and execute strategic pavement data analysis plans, conduct targeted pavement performance case studies, and advance and validate state-of-the art pavement testing technologies. Work also includes developing user-friendly web-based engineering tools for State DOT practitioners, publishing 508-compliant documents and facilitating regional practitioner workshops for technology transfer. Task Area C � Special Research Datasets Development: The Contractor shall develop, update, and curate specialized research datasets for broader highway infrastructure research applications. Work includes establishing automated ingestion pipelines and designing modern database schemas to process, quality-check, and store high-resolution 3D Automated Pavement Condition Survey (3D APCS) and continuous deflection datasets; engineering and refining automated data pipelines to produce clean, reliable, and optimized datasets, machine learning feature stores, and structured data environments to support advanced computational modeling across FHWA InfoHighway platforms; generating, validating, developing, and updating computed parameters required for mechanistic-empirical pavement design and machine learning models; and executing close technical coordination with external InfoHighway web portal support contractors (responsible for web portal administration and hosting) to align data schemas, resolve technical issues, provide technical support to data users and stakeholders, and ensure seamless dataset delivery for public releases and web portal data deployments.

title: 7230--WINDOW TREATMENT
description: Amendment 36C24627Q0113 (P00003) Window Fabric Treatment Questions (Black) / Response (Red) 1. Scope and Quantities The window schedule identifies 96 windows across Pods A, B, C, and D. Amendment 0001 states that the valances will also need fabric. Could the Government confirm whether the 96 scheduled windows represent the complete quantity, and whether valance fabric is included in these quantities or should be priced separately? Response: Valance fabric was included as a full unit to the window. 96 windows = 96 valences. 2. Existing WebbLok Hardware Amendment 0001 indicates that existing WebbLok tracks, brackets, tubes, operators, and valances appear to be in place, except for one missing track in Room S136 Recreation. Could the Government confirm which existing hardware components are expected to be reused and whether the contractor is responsible for replacing the missing track? Response: S136 is not part of this contract. 3. Site Access and Measurements Is there an opportunity for prospective quoters or their proposed installation partners to conduct a pre-award site visit and field measurements? If not, could the Government confirm whether measurements and verification will be permitted immediately after award and before materials are ordered? Response: The measurements is provided in the original solicitation. Government confirms that they will be able to measure prior to ordering as that is listed in the SOW. 4. Installation Phasing and Schedule Could the Government provide an anticipated installation timeframe or expected sequence for Pods A, B, C, and D? Are there any anticipated restrictions on the number of Pods or rooms that may be worked on simultaneously? Response: Installation timeframe is dependent upon the lead time of the fabric offered. Restrictions would include working past 5PM in occupied pods, however, the VA asks to complete rooms all the way through to ensure complete activation (ie: no removing all the blind fabrics and not being able to put it back up by end of day.) 5. Project Experience Requirements The solicitation requires at least five years of healthcare interior design/furniture installation and project management experience, as well as three Federal projects valued at $750,000 or more. Could the Government clarify whether the experience and past-performance qualifications of a proposed subcontractor or installation partner may be considered in satisfying these requirements when the prime contractor is responsible for project management and contract administration? Response: That will qualify. 6. Past Performance Could the Government clarify whether the three Federal projects referenced in the experience requirement must each be valued at $750,000 or more, and whether projects involving window treatment installation or similar healthcare facility interior installations may qualify? Response: Must be valued at $750,000 and similar facility installations qualify. 7. Pricing and Installation The price schedule separates material and installation services by Pod. Could the Government confirm whether installation pricing should include removal and disposal of existing shade fabric, fabric installation on valances, field measurements, project management, training of VA maintenance personnel, cleanup, and punch-list trips Response: Correct, pricing should include installation, measurements, project management, clean-up, and punch list. 8. Product Specification Is the specified Inpro WT Commercial Shade Fabric 25X, 251-10 the required product, or may a technically equivalent product meeting all specified characteristics be offered? If an equivalent product is proposed, could the Government confirm the sample submission process and whether the sample deadline is calculated from the original quotation deadline or the date of actual quote submission? Response: This is addressed in the submission. It is an or equal contract.

title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE AIHA LAB ACCREDITATION
description: The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) in Fort Detrick, MD intends to negotiate on a sole source basis (IAW RFO 12.102(a)) with AMERICAN INDUSTRIAL HYGIENE ASSOCIATION (AIHA) 3120 FAIRVIEW PARK DR STE 360 FALLS CHURCH, VA 22042-4586 as the only responsible source that can provide accreditation through the AIHA LAP of the DCPH-A LAB�s IH analytical methods performed by the LAB and for the enrollment in a Proficiency Testing (PT) sample program for industrial hygiene and environmental lead PTs. This is a Pre-solicitation notice in accordance with RFO 5.101. The service provided by AIHA is the only source that provides DHACA with AIHA Lab Accreditation to support their mission. AIHA LAP provides evaluation and accreditation of IH testing laboratories to ensure that the quality of analytical data used for regulatory purposes meets the regulatory requirements of the IH program. To maintain the AIHA LAP accreditation, the LAB must participate in Proficiency Testing (PT) Program. This involves analyzing PT samples provided by AIHA LAP and reporting the results back to AIHA LAP for evaluation. AIHA LAP then issues a pass/fail report based on the LAB results, and a passing grade is required for the LAB to continue analyzing IH samples. This acquisition is being conducted under simplified acquisition procedures. There are no set-aside restrictions for this requirement. The intended procurement will be classified under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 541990 with a Small Business Size Standard of $19.5 mil. This presolicitation notice is not a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation document exists for this requirement. However, any parties interested in responding to this notice shall submit technical data, including cost, sufficient to determine capability in providing the same service. All capability statements received by closing of this notification of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Based on the above information, the only technically acceptable subscription can be provided by AIHA . Submit email capability statements (using PDF, MS Word, Excel attachments) to Alicia Maldonado Torres at alicia.maldonadotorres.civ@health.mil. Statements are due no later than 12:00 P.M. EST on 2 December 2026. No phone calls will be accepted.

title: Biosequence Search
description: The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) is conducting market research through this Request for Information (RFI) to gather input from industry on commercially available solutions to search biological sequences, such as DNA, RNA, proteins, peptides, antibodies, probes, primers, fragments, variants, and fusion constructs, as well as prior art searches, claimed in patent applications. The USPTO seeks innovative solutions to implement the next-generation biological sequence search system utilizing Super Intelligence (SI)-assisted capabilities to increase the efficiency and quality of biological searches during patent examinations. The USPTO is interested in solutions that meet the objectives outlined in the attached draft Statement of Objectives (SOO). The Government preference is to obtain a turnkey commercial solution with minor tailoring, if applicable. The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. � 2(b)(4)(A). This PTAG Request for Information (RFI) is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the USPTO will use to determine which vendor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency�s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, the solicitation will only be issued to the limited number of qualified vendor(s). Vendors that do not respond to the RFI will not be considered for the alternative competition and will not be eligible to compete as a prime offeror. Submission of an RFI response does not guarantee a vendor�s eligibility to compete for the biosequence search requirement. This PTAG RFI is not a request for competitive proposals. This RFI is not a solicitation and does not constitute a request for quotations or proposals. The USPTO is not seeking or accepting unsolicited proposals. There is no USPTO commitment or implied agreement or understanding as a result of Government action or inaction taken in response to the RFI or the accompanying documents. Telephone calls requesting a solicitation will not be accepted or acknowledged. Participation in this effort is strictly voluntary. No entitlement to payment will arise as a result of submission of a response to the RFI. Any cost for submission of responses or associated activities is at the interested respondent�s risk and interested respondent�s expense. The USPTO is not liable for costs (direct or indirect) associated with the preparation, submission, or responses to this RFI, including any costs associated with any meetings, follow on questions or additional requests for information, if any. USPTO will not reimburse the respondent for any costs incurred in responding to the RFI. See the attached "ACQ-27-0065 - RFI Biosequence Tool" for submission instructions. description: **Q&A posted and incorporated by referance** The objective of this Statement of Work is to conduct and complete the requirements for the 1-153 CAV Pre-Deployment Event with 330 total guests. It is the responsibility of the contractor to ensure all requested requirements are met. Event space, audio/visual (A/V) services, and catering services will be secured by the contractor with oversight from the Yellow Ribbon POC. Date: 9 January 2027 Hours: All convention space must be available for exclusive use from 0600-1500 on Saturday 09 January 2027. Lodging Hours: Hotel lodging must be available for exclusive use from 1700 on Friday 08 January 2027 until check out Sunday 10 January 2027. Location: Panama City Beach, FL The contractor shall provide a facility that will offer the following: parking lot, event space, audio/ visual equipment and technical support, catering and lodging. The contractor shall provide an on-site representative the day prior to the event, during the event, and after the completion of the event. This representative cannot be a member of the venue or hotel, it must come from the contracting agency. The Federal Government is tax exempt. CLIN 0001 - Catering Requirements: 1.0 A catered hot breakfast will be provided for approximately 330 adults. It will be served buffet style from 0700 to 0900 on 9 January 2027. Drink refreshments will remain available to guests until 1100. Buffet will include a hot meal with a minimum of two main entree choices, an assortment of breakfast pastries, and additional, common breakfast items (i.e. granola, yogurt, fruit, etc.). The buffet will also serve beverages including, but not limited to, hot coffee, juice(s), milk, water, and hot tea including sugar and cream. 1.1 Buffet will not serve 'fast food' items (i.e. french toast sticks, waffle tacos, Cinnamon Swirl Toast Breakfast Sandwiches, cheesy cheddar baco-biscuits, etc.). Egg dishes cannot be made from powdered eggs. Food menu items should avoid common allergies (i.e. shellfish) and clearly label allergens when necessary. At least one entree and one side dish must not include cheese. 1.2 The on-site representative is responsible for ensuring that catered food items conform to these requirements. Failure to meet these requirements will incur a claim from the government. 1.3 Catering services will provide flatware, plates, and condiments. With the exception of paper "to-go" coffee cups, plates and/or flatware must not be paper products. Catering services include set-up and clean-up. Flatware is encouraged to be made of a durable plastic that can be trashed after use. 1.4 Catering will be delivered to the event venue, ready to be served at 0700 9 January 2027. CLIN 0002 - Conference Space Requirements: 2.0 Room #1 � Large room for initial assembly to accommodate 330 guests, tables and chairs for seating, a stage, at least one trash can, and water stations. This room will likely need space to stage the catered breakfast and must provide tables so that guests can eat in this space. A scaled diagram of Room #1's set-up must be provided. See CLIN 0003 for Audio/Visual equipment requirements. 2.1 Registration/check-in area � If an in-house registration area is not available, three 6� tables with 6 chairs & two (2) trash cans shall be provided � Available 0600 - 1500, Saturday, 9 January 2027. 2.2 Room #2 - One room large enough to accommodate a capacity of 50 attendees with tables, chairs, and at least one water station. This room should be only a short distance (<2 minute walk) from room #1. This room will be used to host convention workshops and should include A/V equipment in accordance with CLIN 0003. 2.3 Room #3 - 40 6' vendor tables with two chairs at each table and at least one water station shall be provided in this room as the vendor area. The area should be big enough to host approximately 200 standing attendees and 40 6' vendor tables at any given time. This area may be co-located with room #1 or can be adjacent to room #1. Black table linens shall be provided for 10 tables. 2.4 Parking - Parking must be provided for attendees, vendors, and event staff (approximately 300 vehicles). Under no circumstances shall attendees, vendors, or event staff be required to pay for parking. CLIN 0003 - Audio/Visual Requirements: Audio/Visual and Technology Requirements: Cost shall be included in the total bill from the venue. Must NOT be a separate bill. 3.0 Room #1 A/V requirements: � 1 podium with microphone stand � 2 hand microphones with sound system � 1 screen with dimensions at least 6' by 6'. This may be a projector screen. � 1 A/V cart or projector (if needed) � A stage 3.1 Room #2 A/V requirements: � 2 hand microphones with sound system � 1 screen with dimensions at least 6' by 6'. This may be a projector screen. � 1 A/V cart or projector (if needed) A technician must be on site for trouble shooting the day before and the day of event. CLIN 0004 - Lodging Requirements: 4.0 The Federal Government is tax exempt. Vendor accommodations must be within 10 miles of the event venue. Multiple lodging venues may be used to meet this requirement. All lodging venues to be used are subject to the requirements specified in CLIN 0004. The on-site representative must be able to meet Yellow Ribbon staff at the lodging venue(s), if requested. The on-site representative is responsible for ensuring that event-attendees identified by the Yellow Ribbon Coordinator who qualify to receive lodging are able to successfully check-in to the lodging venue without complications. 4.1 Attendees who meet our requirements for lodging will start to arrive the day prior to the event. The amount of rooms required are: � 45 rooms for the night of Friday, 8 January 2027 � 15 rooms for the night of Saturday, 9 January 2027 4.2 Lodging facilities shall meet the American with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements and provide ADA compliant rooms. A preliminary requirement for ADA compliant sleep rooms and special room requirements will be provided by 18 December 2026. 4.3 All rooms provided under this contract shall be non-smoking rooms. The venue will not be undergoing renovations during event dates. Overnight and daily parking will be included in the contract for 45 vehicles on the days/nights of 8-9 January 2027. The parking area must be within walking distance of the lodging venue and not require a shuttle service to the front lobby of the venue. 4.4 Personal Expenses: Personal expenses in guest rooms such as long distance phone charges, movie rentals, laundry, room service, etc. will be paid by the guest and shall not be billed under the resultant contract. NOTE: If cash or credit card is not available, incidental services shall be blocked for use in the room. The lodging venue may not deny qualified or identified event attendees the use of lodging if the attendee does not present a credit card for incidentals. 4.5 The Yellow Ribbon Coordinator may review the offered hotel facilities prior to awarding a contract at his or her discretion. The contractor shall provide facilities that will offer the following: lighted parking lot, an exercise room, functional elevators, and ice machines. The Contractor shall provide an on-site representative to mediate complications and concerns while event attendees check-in and check-out from their rooms and all times between. The on-site representative must be a representative from the contracting agency and cannot be a member of the hotel staff. 4.6 The lodging venue(s) should include a gym/fitness center, 24-hour front desk assistance, business services, a pool, and laundry services. Rooms should be spacious and include showers with warm water, a working refrigerator, free wi-fi, air conditioning and heating, a flat-screen television, furnishings complete with a desk, closet, chair(s), and an alarm clock. Hotel facilities must be free of pests (e.g. cockroaches). 4.7 Most importantly, the venue must be located in a low-crime area where attendees feel saf

title: ISBEE Solicitation: 24/7 Telebehavioral Health Emergency Department Support Services � Great Plains Area.
description: ISBEE Set-Aside � 24/7 Telebehavioral Health Emergency Department Support Services Solicitation No. 75H70627R00006 This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with FAR Part 12, as supplemented by the attached solicitation documents. This announcement and its attachments constitute the solicitation. Proposals are requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation No. 75H70627R00006 is issued as a Request for Proposals (RFP) for 24/7 Telebehavioral Health Emergency Department Support Services. The Great Plains Area Indian Health Service (IHS) seeks a contractor to provide non-personal, synchronous audio-video telebehavioral health services 24 hours per day, seven days per week, including weekends and federal holidays. Initial supported Emergency Departments are Pine Ridge, Rosebud, and Eagle Butte in South Dakota, and Fort Yates and Belcourt in North Dakota. Services include crisis behavioral health assessment, suicide-risk evaluation, safety planning, crisis intervention, placement assistance, interpreter-access coordination, and medication-stabilization consultation by qualified prescribing providers when clinically indicated. The contractor shall furnish qualified licensed personnel, staffing management, backup and surge coverage, credentialing support, and other contractor-furnished resources necessary to perform the Performance Work Statement (PWS) and applicable task orders. This acquisition is set aside exclusively for Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs). The assigned NAICS code is 621112, Offices of Physicians, Mental Health Specialists, with a small business size standard of $13.5 million. Offerors shall satisfy the eligibility and representation requirements in the solicitation and submit the completed IHS Indian Economic Enterprise Representation form with their proposals. The anticipated award is a firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract with one 12-month base ordering period and four 12-month option ordering periods. The anticipated start date for services is August 1, 2027. The anticipated base period is August 1, 2027, through July 31, 2028, with an ordering period extending through July 31, 2032, if all options are exercised. Services will be authorized and funded through written task orders identifying covered facilities, performance periods, and applicable requirements. The contract minimum guarantee is $25,000, and the maximum ordering ceiling is $2,600,000. The ceiling does not represent guaranteed expenditures or orders beyond the contract minimum. Section F of the attached solicitation identifies the CLINs, service descriptions, quantities, units of measure, and performance periods. Offerors shall complete that price schedule with firm-fixed monthly pricing by facility for the base period and each option period. The total evaluated price will include the base period and all four option periods. Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose proposal conforms to the solicitation and represents the best value to the Government. Evaluation factors are Technical Capability, Past Performance, Management Approach, and Price. When combined, the non-price factors are significantly more important than price. The Government intends to award without discussions but reserves the right to conduct discussions as provided in the solicitation. Questions must be received no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon) Central Standard Time (CST) on November 18, 2026. Proposals must be received no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon) CST on December 2, 2026. Submit questions and proposals electronically to David.Jones@ihs.gov, referencing Solicitation No. 75H70627R00006 in the email subject line. Offerors must have a valid Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and active SAM.gov registration as required by the solicitation. Applicable solicitation provisions and contract clauses are identified in the attached provision/clause schedule. Incorporated FAR provisions and clauses are accessible at https://www.acquisition.gov. Review the complete attached solicitation package, including the PWS, price schedule, submission instructions, evaluation criteria, applicable FAR/HHSAR provisions and clauses, and any amendments before submitting a proposal.

title: Z2DA--FY27 EHRM | 657-21-702JC EHRM Training And Administrative Space Construction - St Louis John Cochran
description: INTRODUCTION The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) anticipates soliciting bids and subsequently awarding a single firm-fixed-price contract for the design-bid-build EHRM Training and Administrative Space Construction project at the St. Louis VA Health Care System (VAHCS) John Cochran campus located at 915 North Grand BLVD, St. Louis, MO 63106. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The VA Saint Louis Health Care System John Cochran Division requires a construction contractor to perform upgrades in support of the Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) program. The construction area is located on the first floor of Building 2 and includes both training and administrative spaces. This project includes the execution of Phases 2, 3, and 4 of the associated design plans. Phase 2 addresses the North Training Rooms (Rooms 139, 140, 141, 142), totaling approximately 2,000 square feet. Work includes upgraded power and data infrastructure and new flooring and wall finishes. Phase 3 addresses the South Training Rooms (Rooms 126, 127, 128), totaling approximately 1,800 square feet. Work includes upgraded power and data infrastructure and new flooring and wall finishes. Additionally, Phase 3 includes the renovation of a 130-square-foot breakroom, with new floor and wall finishes, casework, a new sink, and a cold-water tie-in for an ice machine. Phase 4 addresses multiple areas: renovation of an approximately 1,400-square-foot corridor with new floor and wall finishes; upgrades to two offices (approximately 150 square feet each) with upgraded power and data infrastructure and new flooring and wall finishes; and upgrades to an existing data closet, including new floor and wall finishes, installation of an additional server rack with associated equipment, and replacement of the existing mini-split HVAC unit. Note: Phase 1 is excluded from this scope, as it was completed under a separate contract. Note: All power and data drops originally indicated as floor-mounted shall now be wall-mounted, as shown on revised drawings EP101 and TN101. Installation must match these updated sheet details; no floor-mounted outlets are permitted. ADMINISTRATIVE The solicitation will be issued as an Invitation for Bids (IFB) conducted in accordance with FAR part 14 and will be evaluated in accordance with the procedures listed in the solicitation. The solicitation will be issued as a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Offers received from other than SDVOSB concerns will not be considered. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 with a size standard of $45.0 million. The solicitation will be issued in early to mid-October 2026. The period of performance is approximately 150 calendar days from the issuance of the notice to proceed. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $250,000 and $500,000. This notice is not a request for competitive offers. All questions must be submitted in writing to the issuing office via email to Amanda.Webster@va.gov. Telephone calls will not be accepted.

description: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Center for Domestic Preparedness (CDP), requires Armed Security Guard Services as described in the attached Statement of Work (SOW) 1 This RFI has been developed to solicit market research information from industry. THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY. The purpose of this RFI is to identify sources, collect information on socio-economic status and receive industry comments on the draft Statement of Work (SOW) including (but not limited to) technical questions and comments, contract pricing considerations and contract type for the competitively contracted services for Armed Security Guard Services for the Center for Domestic Preparedness in Anniston, Alabama. The CDP is a national training facility located in Anniston, Alabama that prepares state and local emergency response personnel to respond to all-hazards, including terrorist attacks using weapons of mass destruction, by providing advanced, hands-on training. This national training program was developed for state, local, tribal, Federal, private sector and international responders from Fire Service, Law Enforcement, Emergency Medical Services, Emergency Management, HazMat, Public Health, Healthcare, Public Communications, Public Works and Government Administrative and other emergency response personnel, their trainers and supervisors. Training courses at the CDP provide specific knowledge and expertise for deterrence, prevention and response to Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear and Explosive (CBRNE) incidents; mass casualty incidents; and incidents involving hazardous materials by providing advanced, hands-on and classroom-based state-of-the-art training. Armed Security Guard Services, as described in the attached draft SOW, includes but is not limited to providing properly qualified, trained, licensed, armed and certified personnel, their uniforms, equipment, tools, materials, supervision and other items and services except such equipment and supplies as provided by the Government necessary to: (1) plan for, and (2) provide continuous (24 hours per day, 7 days per week) static post and roving patrol armed security services to protect the CDP enclave; participation in site security surveys and inspections; provide operation and monitoring of the CDP security Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) and Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS); monitor fire alarm systems; participation in planning for and execution of CDP and Chemical, Ordnance, Biological, and Radiological Training Facility (COBRATF) Emergency Response Exercise (ERP) actions; performing visual inspection/security checks, via motorized and foot patrol of the CDP enclaves, and a full range of management duties including, but not limited to: planning, scheduling, and quality control. title: Z2DA--FY27 EHRM | 657-21-702JC EHRM Training And Administrative Space Construction - St Louis John Cochran
description: INTRODUCTION The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) anticipates soliciting bids and subsequently awarding a single firm-fixed-price contract for the design-bid-build EHRM Training and Administrative Space Construction project at the St. Louis VA Health Care System (VAHCS) John Cochran campus located at 915 North Grand BLVD, St. Louis, MO 63106. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The VA Saint Louis Health Care System John Cochran Division requires a construction contractor to perform upgrades in support of the Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) program. The construction area is located on the first floor of Building 2 and includes both training and administrative spaces. This project includes the execution of Phases 2, 3, and 4 of the associated design plans. Phase 2 addresses the North Training Rooms (Rooms 139, 140, 141, 142), totaling approximately 2,000 square feet. Work includes upgraded power and data infrastructure and new flooring and wall finishes. Phase 3 addresses the South Training Rooms (Rooms 126, 127, 128), totaling approximately 1,800 square feet. Work includes upgraded power and data infrastructure and new flooring and wall finishes. Additionally, Phase 3 includes the renovation of a 130-square-foot breakroom, with new floor and wall finishes, casework, a new sink, and a cold-water tie-in for an ice machine. Phase 4 addresses multiple areas: renovation of an approximately 1,400-square-foot corridor with new floor and wall finishes; upgrades to two offices (approximately 150 square feet each) with upgraded power and data infrastructure and new flooring and wall finishes; and upgrades to an existing data closet, including new floor and wall finishes, installation of an additional server rack with associated equipment, and replacement of the existing mini-split HVAC unit. Note: Phase 1 is excluded from this scope, as it was completed under a separate contract. Note: All power and data drops originally indicated as floor-mounted shall now be wall-mounted, as shown on revised drawings EP101 and TN101. Installation must match these updated sheet details; no floor-mounted outlets are permitted. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $250,000 and $500,000. This notice is not a request for competitive offers. All questions must be submitted in writing to the issuing office via email to Amanda.Webster@va.gov. Telephone calls will not be accepted.

title: Yellow Ribbon Post-Deployment Event For 1-153 CAV
description: The objective of this Statement of Work is to conduct and complete the requirements for the 1-153 CAV Pre-Deployment Event with 330 total guests. It is the responsibility of the contractor to ensure all requested requirements are met. Event space, audio/visual (A/V) services, and catering services will be secured by the contractor with oversight from the Yellow Ribbon POC. Date: 9 January 2027 Hours: All convention space must be available for exclusive use from 0600-1500 on Saturday 09 January 2027. Lodging Hours: Hotel lodging must be available for exclusive use from 1700 on Friday 08 January 2027 until check out Sunday 10 January 2027. Location: Panama City Beach, FL The contractor shall provide a facility that will offer the following: parking lot, event space, audio/ visual equipment and technical support, catering and lodging. The contractor shall provide an on-site representative the day prior to the event, during the event, and after the completion of the event. This representative cannot be a member of the venue or hotel, it must come from the contracting agency. The Federal Government is tax exempt. CLIN 0001 - Catering Requirements: 1.0 A catered hot breakfast will be provided for approximately 330 adults. It will be served buffet style from 0700 to 0900 on 9 January 2027. Drink refreshments will remain available to guests until 1100. Buffet will include a hot meal with a minimum of two main entree choices, an assortment of breakfast pastries, and additional, common breakfast items (i.e. granola, yogurt, fruit, etc.). The buffet will also serve beverages including, but not limited to, hot coffee, juice(s), milk, water, and hot tea including sugar and cream. 1.1 Buffet will not serve 'fast food' items (i.e. french toast sticks, waffle tacos, Cinnamon Swirl Toast Breakfast Sandwiches, cheesy cheddar baco-biscuits, etc.). Egg dishes cannot be made from powdered eggs. Food menu items should avoid common allergies (i.e. shellfish) and clearly label allergens when necessary. At least one entree and one side dish must not include cheese. 1.2 The on-site representative is responsible for ensuring that catered food items conform to these requirements. Failure to meet these requirements will incur a claim from the government. 1.3 Catering services will provide flatware, plates, and condiments. With the exception of paper "to-go" coffee cups, plates and/or flatware must not be paper products. Catering services include set-up and clean-up. Flatware is encouraged to be made of a durable plastic that can be trashed after use. 1.4 Catering will be delivered to the event venue, ready to be served at 0700 9 January 2027. CLIN 0002 - Conference Space Requirements: 2.0 Room #1 � Large room for initial assembly to accommodate 330 guests, tables and chairs for seating, a stage, at least one trash can, and water stations. This room will likely need space to stage the catered breakfast and must provide tables so that guests can eat in this space. A scaled diagram of Room #1's set-up must be provided. See CLIN 0003 for Audio/Visual equipment requirements. 2.1 Registration/check-in area � If an in-house registration area is not available, three 6� tables with 6 chairs & two (2) trash cans shall be provided � Available 0600 - 1500, Saturday, 9 January 2027. 2.2 Room #2 - One room large enough to accommodate a capacity of 50 attendees with tables, chairs, and at least one water station. This room should be only a short distance (<2 minute walk) from room #1. This room will be used to host convention workshops and should include A/V equipment in accordance with CLIN 0003. 2.3 Room #3 - 40 6' vendor tables with two chairs at each table and at least one water station shall be provided in this room as the vendor area. The area should be big enough to host approximately 200 standing attendees and 40 6' vendor tables at any given time. This area may be co-located with room #1 or can be adjacent to room #1. Black table linens shall be provided for 10 tables. 2.4 Parking - Parking must be provided for attendees, vendors, and event staff (approximately 300 vehicles). Under no circumstances shall attendees, vendors, or event staff be required to pay for parking. CLIN 0003 - Audio/Visual Requirements: Audio/Visual and Technology Requirements: Cost shall be included in the total bill from the venue. Must NOT be a separate bill. 3.0 Room #1 A/V requirements: � 1 podium with microphone stand � 2 hand microphones with sound system � 1 screen with dimensions at least 6' by 6'. This may be a projector screen. � 1 A/V cart or projector (if needed) � A stage 3.1 Room #2 A/V requirements: � 2 hand microphones with sound system � 1 screen with dimensions at least 6' by 6'. This may be a projector screen. � 1 A/V cart or projector (if needed) A technician must be on site for trouble shooting the day before and the day of event. CLIN 0004 - Lodging Requirements: 4.0 The Federal Government is tax exempt. Vendor accommodations must be within 10 miles of the event venue. Multiple lodging venues may be used to meet this requirement. All lodging venues to be used are subject to the requirements specified in CLIN 0004. The on-site representative must be able to meet Yellow Ribbon staff at the lodging venue(s), if requested. The on-site representative is responsible for ensuring that event-attendees identified by the Yellow Ribbon Coordinator who qualify to receive lodging are able to successfully check-in to the lodging venue without complications. 4.1 Attendees who meet our requirements for lodging will start to arrive the day prior to the event. The amount of rooms required are: � 45 rooms for the night of Friday, 8 January 2027 � 15 rooms for the night of Saturday, 9 January 2027 4.2 Lodging facilities shall meet the American with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements and provide ADA compliant rooms. A preliminary requirement for ADA compliant sleep rooms and special room requirements will be provided by 18 December 2026. 4.3 All rooms provided under this contract shall be non-smoking rooms. The venue will not be undergoing renovations during event dates. Overnight and daily parking will be included in the contract for 45 vehicles on the days/nights of 8-9 January 2027. The parking area must be within walking distance of the lodging venue and not require a shuttle service to the front lobby of the venue. 4.4 Personal Expenses: Personal expenses in guest rooms such as long distance phone charges, movie rentals, laundry, room service, etc. will be paid by the guest and shall not be billed under the resultant contract. NOTE: If cash or credit card is not available, incidental services shall be blocked for use in the room. The lodging venue may not deny qualified or identified event attendees the use of lodging if the attendee does not present a credit card for incidentals. 4.5 The Yellow Ribbon Coordinator may review the offered hotel facilities prior to awarding a contract at his or her discretion. The contractor shall provide facilities that will offer the following: lighted parking lot, an exercise room, functional elevators, and ice machines. The Contractor shall provide an on-site representative to mediate complications and concerns while event attendees check-in and check-out from their rooms and all times between. The on-site representative must be a representative from the contracting agency and cannot be a member of the hotel staff. 4.6 The lodging venue(s) should include a gym/fitness center, 24-hour front desk assistance, business services, a pool, and laundry services. Rooms should be spacious and include showers with warm water, a working refrigerator, free wi-fi, air conditioning and heating, a flat-screen television, furnishings complete with a desk, closet, chair(s), and an alarm clock. Hotel facilities must be free of pests (e.g. cockroaches). 4.7 Most importantly, the venue must be located in a low-crime area where attendees feel safe walking alone at night. The Yellow Ribbon C

title: Commercial Gear Backup Power (CGBP) and Control System Improvements at Fish Barrier
description: I. PURPOSE AND DISCLAIMER**********************The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Chicago District, is issuing this sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support the requirement for upgrading our Commercial Gear Backup Power (CGBP) and associated control system at our electronic fish barrier located in Romeoville, Illinois. We are seeking to identify qualified Small Business concerns (including 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, and Small Business Joint Ventures/Teaming Arrangements) and Other-Than-Small Business concerns capable of performing this requirement. The intention is to procure these services on a competitive basis.**********************BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/MARKET RESEARCH, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SMALL BUSINESSES (IN FULL OR IN PART) OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION, and multiple awards MAY be made. All Small Business Set-Aside categories will be considered. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions.**********************DISCLAIMER**********************THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) TO BE SUBMITTED. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. RESPPONSES WILL NOT BE RETURNED TO THE RESPONDER. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) OR RFP, IF ANY ISSUED. IF A SOLICITATION IS RELEASED, IT WILL BE SYNOPSIZED ON THE GOVERNMENT-WIDE POINT OF ENTRY (GPE). IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO MONITOR THE GPE FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMMATION PERTAINING TO THIS REQUIREMENT. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this Sources Sought.********************************************II. COMPREHENSIVE TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION and PROJECT SCOPE********************************************The Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) Electric Dispersal Barrier facility requires a complex industrial electrical power generation, backup power, and automation and control system modernization project. This system is a critical component of the federal effort to prevent the movement of invasive aquatic species between the Great Lakes and Mississippi River basins. **********************Specifically, USACE needs to upgrade the backup generator and switchgear control systems at Permanent Barrier 1 (PB1) to correct unreliable operation caused by deficiencies in the original design, configuration, and wiring. The project requires replacing generator controllers, modernizing breaker controls and communications, and rebuilding the control software and operator interfaces to improve reliable operation on utility and backup power. Work will require testing, operator training, and a phased changeover to maintain continuous barrier operations. Work will be performed at an active, mission-critical facility requiring careful coordination with ongoing operations, planned equipment outages, and system changeovers to maintain operational readiness and minimize disruptions. A critical requirement is the integration of new equipment into an active industrial facility while protecting existing operations. The anticipated work may include engineering, design review, equipment upgrades and replacement, control system programming, integration, testing, and commissioning of interconnected electrical and industrial automation systems. ******************************************************************TECHNICAL CAPABILITIES:******************************************************************The project requires specialized expertise in: a) generator synchronization and load management, b) switchgear automation, c) protective relaying, d) programmable logic controllers (PLCs), e) human-machine interfaces (HMIs), industrial communications, and associated monitoring and data management systems.**********************Contractors must possess the technical capabilities necessary to work with the existing systems and integrate new equipment while maintaining compatibility and functionality. The existing facility incorporates Rockwell Automation ControlLogix PLCs, FactoryTalk View SE, FactoryTalk Transaction Manager, Microsoft SQL Server, Basler generator synchronization and control equipment, Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories (SEL) protective relays and RTAC equipment, and DEIF generator controllers. ATTACHMENT NOTICE: Interested parties must carefully review Attachment 1 (Equipment_SOW.xlsx ??? PB1 Equipment Modernization and SOW Matrix) attached to this notice in PIEE, the DoW Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment, which details the specific equipment removals, modifications, additions, hard-wired control conversions, I/O transitions, and as-built drawing updates (across four separate contractor drawing sets) required under our anticipated scope.**********************Contractors must demonstrate their capability of obtaining a specialized Master Systems Integrator (MSI) or Industrial Automation and Control Systems (IACS) engineering firm to perform any needed engineering, programming, integration, testing, commissioning, and troubleshooting of the complex interconnected industrial control systems.**********************Contractors must demonstrate their ability to obtain qualified personnel. Qualified personnel include Electrical Generating Systems Association (EGSA) certified technicians or personnel possessing equivalent documented qualifications to support generator-related engineering, design reviews, integration, testing, and commissioning. If proposing to use equivalent, provide what documentation your firm considers as equivalent for USACE consideration.**********************The contractor must possess the technical and organizational capabilities to execute phased modifications, coordinate authorized shutdowns and system changeovers, implement temporary control arrangements where necessary, perform pre-commissioning and acceptance testing, and develop contingency measures to minimize operational disruptions and maintain the safety, reliability, and continuity of existing barrier operations.**********************III. REQUESTED INFORMATION FROM INTERESTED PARTIES********************************************Interested firms are invited to submit a Capability Statement (not to exceed 10 pages) addressing the following four (4) sections after reviewing the technical capability narrative above and Attachment 1 (Equipment_SOW.xlsx):SECTION A: ADMINISTRATIVE AND BUSINESS SIZE********************************************1. Company Name, Address, Point of Contact, telephone number and email, CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI).**********************2. Business Size under NAICS 238210 ($19.0M Size Standard) and all applicable socioeconomic designations.**********************3. If proposing as a Small Business, confirm your understanding of FAR 52.219-14 (Limitations on Subcontracting) and your ability to perform at least 25% of the cost of contract performance (excluding the cost of materials) with your own organization or similarly situated small business entities. **********************4. Should this requirement be solicited as Full and Open Competition, other-than-small-business offerors will be required to submit an acceptable Small Business Subcontracting Plan in accordance with RFO 19.1

title: Small Arms Fire Control - Basic Capability Industry Day
description: SPECIAL NOTICE Call for Participants � Product Manager Soldier Weapons Small Arms Fire Control � Basic Capability Industry Day *Updated 19 NOV 2026 - Changes identified with an asterisk. Notice ID: TBD Document Type: Special Notice Response Date: 02 December 2026 NLT 1400EST Classification Code: TBD PSC: 1240 � Optical Sighting and Ranging Equipment NAICS: 332994 � Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing This notice serves as a notification for the event. All dates presented in this notice are estimates and are subject to change. Small Arms Fire Control � Basic Capability (SAFC � BC): The USG will host a SAFC � BC Industry Day on 08 December 2026 from 0800-1600 EST, to provide Program Overview, review draft acquisition strategy, and share USG information. A No-Host Social will follow the event. The SAFC � BC Industry Day will be held at Hilton Garden Inn � Rockaway (375 Mount Hope Ave., Rockaway NJ 07866 (973-328-0600)). Group rate available in limited quantity. The SAFC - BC system is envisioned as commercial/non-developmental weapon-mounted standalone reflexive/holographic sight with magnifier, as well as an aiming laser. The system will combine the close range, rapid target engagement capabilities of the M68 Close Combat Optic (CCO), the magnified capabilities of the M150 Rifle Combat Optic (RCO) and the aiming laser capabilities of a PEQ-15 - all while being able to withstand mechanical stress profiles created by weapon recoil and conform to MIL-STD-810 environmental conditions. Attendance at the Industry Day is limited and requires Government approval. All visitors will be required to fill in and submit the required form(s) identified below on or before 02 December 2026. For security purposes there will be no walk-ins or unregistered visitors allowed. There will be no one-on-one sessions the day of the event, but there will be opportunity for interested parties to sign up for a session. Detailed information will be in the Welcome Packet which will be provided upon RSVP. All participating companies will be required to provide the two following documents: 1. A Non-disclosure Agreement (NDA); and 2. an Attendee List including name and email prior to attending the event. By signing the NDA, attendees agree to use such information only for purposes authorized in connection with the meeting and not to disclose it to any third party without prior written authorization. See Attachment section of this Special Notice for blank NDA Form and use the following fill-ins: Contract No.: N/A Solicitation No.: PANDTA-27-P-0000 041362 *IMPORTANT: A signed/approved DD2345 is required for attendance. A blank DD2345 is attached and detailed instructions, in addition to those in the form, can be found at DLA.mil. For foreign companies, non-US citizens, and/or US citizens representing foreign companies, please provide your name, country of citizenship, and company to the POC below and further registration directions will be provided. Notes: (a) The USG does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this Special Notice or to otherwise pay for the information solicited except as an allowable cost under other contracts as provided in subsection 31.205-18, bid and proposal costs, of the Federal Acquisition Regulation. title: Registration, Storage and Distribution of Chemicals and Drugs for Pre-Clinical Discovery Evaluation and Development
description: This Sources Sought Notice is issued as a means of conducting market research to identify any/all parties, to include large and small businesses, having an interest in and the resources to support the requirements for Registration, Storage and Distribution of Chemicals and Drugs for Pre-Clinical Discovery Evaluation and Development. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. Interested parties are expected to review this notice and the draft Statement of Work (SOW) to familiarize themselves with the requirement of this project; failure to do so will be at your firm�s own risk. The Drug Synthesis and Chemistry Branch (DSCB) of the Developmental Therapeutics Program (DTP) of the Division of Cancer Treatment and Diagnosis (DCTD) of the National Cancer Institute (NCI) is seeking support services to operate and maintain the National Cancer Institute�s Chemotherapeutic Agents Repository (NCI-CAR). This acquisition is responsible for providing an informational interface with NCI and external investigators that are submitting or requesting research compounds; for updating of the chemical database which includes chemical, inventory, receiving and shipping information; systematic file and record keeping of both current and archival information related to repository activities; and reacquisition of samples for continued chemical and biological studies. Towards this goal, the Program acquires and evaluates about 5,000 single agents each year in anticancer assays. In addition, research samples are provided to the general research community both in vialed and plated format. NCI-CAR is responsible for receiving, storage and distribution services along with curating an inventory of approximately 500,000 - 600,000 individual samples and associated chemical, inventory and distribution data. Approximately 400 samples are received monthly, registered and shipped to NCI testing facilities; an additional 2,500 samples are weighed monthly from inventory and shipped to research investigators both in the U.S. (including NCI) and foreign countries. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to identify all potentially capable, interested sources. We encourage you to respond to this Sources Sought Notice; particularly if you are a small business. All Small Business Set-Aside categories will be considered. As a result of this Sources Sought notice, the NCI may issue a Request for Proposal (RFP). THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. However, should such a requirement materialize, no basis for claim against the NCI shall arise as a result of a response to this Sources Sought Notice or the NCI�s use of such information as either part of our evaluation process or in developing specification for any subsequent requirement.

title: Maintenance Dredging of New York and New Jersey Harbor � Arthur Kill 50 foot Reach Federal Navigation Project
description: Market Survey Background Information The New York District of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) proposes to perform maintenance dredging of the New York and New Jersey Harbor � Arthur Kill 50 foot Reach Federal Navigation Project to a depth of -50 feet Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) plus 1 foot of allowable over-depth. The proposed maintenance dredging would remove approximately 150,000 cubic yards (CY) of material from the critical shoal area. The dredged material would be dredged and subsequently placed at a suitable, contractor provided, state permitted upland placement site(s). The dredged material is expected to consist primarily of silt, clay, and some sand. Based on the past dredging projects within the New York Harbor, and anticipated restrictions found in the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation Water Quality Certificate, the proposed work can only be performed by utilizing a mechanical clamshell dredge with environmental bucket. Additionally, tug-boats, sealed hull barges and survey vessels will be needed to perform the work during the dredging, transport, processing and placement activities. The dredging, transport and placement at a suitable, contractor provided, state permitted upland placement site(s) would be required to meet all federal, state, and local criteria required by the government agencies having jurisdiction where the dredging and placement sites are located. All necessary permits required for the dredged material placement will be provided by the contractor to the government. The apparent low bidder shall, within 35 calendar days from the date the apparent low bidder is notified of being such, provide copies of all required permits and approvals for transportation, transfer, dewatering, processing, and final placement of dredged material, and shall submit evidence of such permits and approvals to the government. Once the contract is awarded, the contractor will be required to commence work within five (5) calendar days after the date of receipt of the Notice to Proceed and maintain an integrated production rate of at least 3,000 cubic yards per calendar day for the dredging and placement of the dredged material. The presence of the dredging equipment in the channel will impact ship traffic, and it is necessary to maintain this production rate while minimizing the duration of this impact. The proposed work is anticipated to take place in the summer / fall of 2027. SURVEY OF THE DREDGING INDUSTRY The following confidential survey questionnaire is designed to apprise USACE of prospective dredging contractors� project execution capabilities. Please provide your response to the following questions. All questions are in regard to the Arthur Kill 50 foot Reach maintenance dredging project. General 1. Have you ever worked on dredging jobs similar in nature to this project? If so, please describe the project and for whom the work was performed. Identify a point of contact and phone number, as a reference of relevant experience. 2. Have you performed dredging within the waters of the Port of New York and New Jersey? 3. Do you have experience with the placement of dredged material at a suitable, contractor provided, state permitted upland placement site? Please list your experience. 4. What percentage of work (volume of material dredged, transported, processed and ultimately placed) can you perform with your own equipment or equipment owned by another dredging contractor? 5. Would you be willing to bid on the project previously described? If the answer is No, please explain why not. 6. Would you be bidding on this project as a sole contractor, prime contractor with subcontractor(s) or as a joint venture? 7. Is there a dollar limit on the size of contract that you would bid? If so, what is that limit? 8. What is the largest dredging contract, in dollars, on which you were the prime contractor? 9. What is your bonding capacity per contract? What is your total bonding capacity? 10. Do you have experience using USACE Resident Management System (RMS) 3.0 for delivering Submittals, Daily Dredging Reports and Pay Estimates? 11. In the event that the USACE transitions from Resident Management System (RMS) to an alternative construction management system during the contract, will the contractor be ready to adapt to the new management system? 12. Do you have experience applying USACE EM 385-1-1 (Mar 2024) and all requirements? Deficiencies observed on site will require immediate attention and action to meet all applicable safety codes. Equipment 13. What type of dredge equipment do you own and/or operate that is suitable for the work described? Do you own a mechanical dredge with a closed environmental clamshell bucket? Please list each piece of equipment capable of performing the work described, i.e. dredging, transfer, transportation, processing and final placement of the material. For each dredge that you list, please specify its bucket size(s), and any other salient characteristics. 14. Identify which dredge(s), including support equipment (tug, crew boat, scows, etc.), you would employ on this project. Also, for each dredge, identify the maximum dredging depth. 15. Do you own material scows? If so, how many do you have available for use? Please list the name of the scow, its type (ocean-going, sealed hull, etc) and the capacity. 16. Do you have the capability to process the dredged material on your own? If so please explain. If not, what commercial provider of dredge material processing will you engage for this project? What is the daily processing capacity in either case? 17. Will you be able to meet a production rate of 3,000 cubic yards per calendar day and complete all work? 18. Do you have experience with the use of an automated Dredged Material Monitoring System (Black Box / Silent Inspector) employing a Dredged Material Inspector (DMI)?

title: Small Arms Fire Control - Basic Capability Industry Day
description: SPECIAL NOTICE Call for Participants � Product Manager Soldier Weapons Small Arms Fire Control � Basic Capability Industry Day *Updated 19 NOV 2026 - Changes identified with an asterisk. Notice ID: TBD Document Type: Special Notice Response Date: 02 December 2026 NLT 1400EST Classification Code: TBD PSC: 1240 � Optical Sighting and Ranging Equipment NAICS: 332994 � Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing This notice serves as a notification for the event. All dates presented in this notice are estimates and are subject to change. Small Arms Fire Control � Basic Capability (SAFC � BC): The USG will host a SAFC � BC Industry Day on 08 December 2026 from 0800-1600 EST, to provide Program Overview, review draft acquisition strategy, and share USG information. A No-Host Social will follow the event. The SAFC � BC Industry Day will be held at Hilton Garden Inn � Rockaway (375 Mount Hope Ave., Rockaway NJ 07866 (973-328-0600)). Group rate available in limited quantity. The SAFC - BC system is envisioned as commercial/non-developmental weapon-mounted standalone reflexive/holographic sight with magnifier, as well as an aiming laser. The system will combine the close range, rapid target engagement capabilities of the M68 Close Combat Optic (CCO), the magnified capabilities of the M150 Rifle Combat Optic (RCO) and the aiming laser capabilities of a PEQ-15 - all while being able to withstand mechanical stress profiles created by weapon recoil and conform to MIL-STD-810 environmental conditions. Attendance at the Industry Day is limited and requires Government approval. All visitors will be required to fill in and submit the required form(s) identified below on or before 02 December 2026. For security purposes there will be no walk-ins or unregistered visitors allowed. There will be no one-on-one sessions the day of the event, but there will be opportunity for interested parties to sign up for a session. Detailed information will be in the Welcome Packet which will be provided upon RSVP. All participating companies will be required to provide the two following documents: 1. A Non-disclosure Agreement (NDA); and 2. an Attendee List including name and email prior to attending the event. By signing the NDA, attendees agree to use such information only for purposes authorized in connection with the meeting and not to disclose it to any third party without prior written authorization. See Attachment section of this Special Notice for blank NDA Form and use the following fill-ins: Contract No.: N/A Solicitation No.: PANDTA-27-P-0000 041362 *IMPORTANT: A signed/approved DD2345 is required for attendance. Instructions can be found at DLA.mil. For foreign companies, non-US citizens, and/or US citizens representing foreign companies, please provide your name, country of citizenship, and company to the POC below and further registration directions will be provided. Notes: (a) The USG does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this Special Notice or to otherwise pay for the information solicited except as an allowable cost under other contracts as provided in subsection 31.205-18, bid and proposal costs, of the Federal Acquisition Regulation. (b) Although "proposal", "offeror", �respondent�, �contractor� or �industry� may be used in this Special Notice, your response will be treated as information only. It shall not be used as a proposal. (c) This Special Notice is issued for the purpose of informing Industry regarding future contracting plans and soliciting feedback. (d) No award is intended as a result of this Special Notice nor does the USG intend to pay for information received. Any response to this notice is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the USG to form a binding contract. (e) There are no vendor costs to participate in this event. A lack of participation in the SAFC - BC Industry Day does not preclude participation in any future solicitations, if any are issued. (f) The USG will not be responsible for any expenses incurred by a vendor�s decision to participate in the SAFC - BC Industry Day. (g) Vendors will not be notified of the results of this Industry Day. The submission of your signed NDA and Attandee List to the below contacts will be your RSVP. The Point of Contact (POC) is Chad A. Irvine, Contract Specialist, US Army Contracting Command - Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA), and can be contacted via e-mail: chad.a.irvine.civ@army.mil; please also include: Kelly Harp, Contract Specialist, ACC-DTA, kelly.j.harp.civ@army.mil in all communications.

title: Request for Information: U.S. Shipyard and Vessel Construction Manager Capability for Floating Drydock Construction
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is conducting market research to identify qualified U.S.-based shipyards and Vessel Construction Managers (VCMs) capable of supporting the detailed production design, construction, testing, and delivery of a new 8,000 long-ton capacity floating drydock (FDD) before calendar year 2030. The Government anticipates awarding a Firm-Fixed-Price contract through a prime VCM, who will partner with a qualified domestic shipyard to execute the build under American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) survey and classification based on a Government-furnished contract design. Interested parties are encouraged to review the attached Request for Information (RFI) and submit responses in accordance with the instructions provided.
